messages:
Ben G.: Heads-up: saw a small class of double-charges when sampler heartbeats coincide with a fallback route. Happens on streaming requests with midstream model swap.
Priya (platform): Can you paste an example trace?
Ben G.: Betti reproducer attached in logs. Short snippet:
```json
{"session":"s-123","event":"heartbeat","route":"canary","tokens":27}
{"session":"s-123","event":"fallback","route":"stable","tokens":12}
```
Ben G.: Our meter counts both partial stream tokens on the pre-fallback route *and* the initial tokens on the fallback toolcall. So client gets charged for overlapping token ranges.
Alex P.: Hmm. Is this the same as the 'prefix ownership' problem or different because of sampler heartbeats? I thought prefix moved with handoff.
Jamal: Different: sampler heartbeat emits periodic sample tokens for QoS, they end up in the provisional ledger for the original route. When a fallback happens we create a new toolcall session and the ledger includes both. Need to reconcile provisional->confirmed semantics.
Priya (platform): Could be a race in the handoff where provisional tokens are not tombstoned when fallback confirms and they get copied. Any RPC traces?
Ben G.: Yes. Full trace (filtered):
[2026-03-19T12:04:11Z] route=canary session=s-123 event=heartbeat tokens=27 provisional=true
[2026-03-19T12:04:12Z] route=canary session=s-123 event=prefetch tokens=8 provisional=true
[2026-03-19T12:04:13Z] route=stable session=s-234 event=fallback-start toolcall=start
[2026-03-19T12:04:13Z] route=stable session=s-234 event=toolcall tokens=12 confirmed=true
[2026-03-19T12:04:13Z] ledger=write session=s-123 tokens_added=27
[2026-03-19T12:04:13Z] ledger=write session=s-234 tokens_added=12
Alex P.: So ledger writes before the tombstone path wins. We should mark provisional tokens with a session ownership id that can be deduped on fallback. But that may break streaming UX.
Laura S.: Ops-bot alerted this morning to a tiny billing spike for a single tenant. I checked, it's exactly this pattern.
ops-bot: [alert] Billing anomaly detected for customer cust-77 — +0.4% token delta last hour.
Jamal: Proposal: on fallback confirmation we emit a 'reclaim' op that marks overlapping provisional tokens as tombstoned, and ledger will ignore tombstoned ranges when confirm write happens.
Priya (platform): Reclaim op sounds fine. Do we have existing tombstone flow? I worry about adding another async op that might itself race.
Ben G.: We already have tombstone in snapshot GC flow but it's not tied to immediate fallback confirmation. We need a synchronous small reconcile path.
Alex P.: Could also use idempotent token ranges: attach a provenance ID to each token range, and confirm write will set a 'confirmed_by' and ledger dedupes when same provenance appears. Simpler to reason but requires ledger change.
Jamal: My vote: quick pragmatic fix = when fallback triggers, pause the canary provisional flush for 200ms for that session, then perform canonical confirm+reclaim inline. We'll add metrics for timeouts so we don't stall too long.
Priya (platform): I like starting conservative. Add a console UX change: show 'recent tombstone events' per session so CS can inspect. Also add a dashboard alert for overlapping provisional vs confirmed token percent.
Ben G.: I'll prototype the 200ms pause + inline reclaim. PR will include tests covering race with sampler heartbeat.
Alex P.: Add a unit test that simulates heartbeat at t0, fallback at t0+1ms, ensure ledger ends with max(tokens) not sum.
Laura S.: Ops: contact cust-77 support, offer reconciliation and credit if we confirm double-charge. I'll draft note.
ops-bot: [reminder] follow-up in 3d for PR and ops reconciliation.
Ben G.: Filing a ticket now: INF-11849. I'll ping when PR is up.
Priya (platform): Thank you. Keep it lightweight; we should avoid large ledger refactors for now.
Jamal: Sounds good. If the pause causes regressions we can iterate to the provenance-based dedupe.
Alex P.: Cool. Thanks all :thumbsup:
